title: Design Splitwise (Expense Sharing)
relevance: High — staple LLD / machine-coding question (campus + experienced); tests Strategy for split types, pairwise balance ledgers, debt simplification, and concurrency at Flipkart, Uber, Amazon, Microsoft, Atlassian, and fintech loops (Razorpay / CRED / PhonePe style).
company_notes: Campus/machine-coding staple at Flipkart, Uber, Swiggy, Amazon new-grad, and Indian product cos (working EQUAL/EXACT/PERCENT + balances in ~90 min; simplify as stretch). Experienced LLD at FAANG / Atlassian / Microsoft / fintech probes Strategy vs switch, pairwise ledger correctness, greedy vs optimal simplify, and concurrent balance updates. Among the top ~10 canonical LLD problems.

phases.goal: Lock FRs/NFRs and assumptions: split types, pairwise balances, settle/simplify scope, single currency, and what is out of scope.

must_hit.point: Support users and groups; add expense with payer, amount, participants, and split type EQUAL / EXACT / PERCENT; show pairwise balances; settle full or partial.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Candidate lists users/groups, addExpense with those fields, showBalances, and settleUp including partial settle.

must_hit.point: Clarify scope early: group and non-group expenses, whether simplify debts and notifications are in scope, concurrency, and single currency.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Asks clarifying questions before designing and states assumptions such as single currency and immutable expenses.

must_hit.point: NFRs: correct validation and rounding, no lost balances under concurrent updates, OCP for new split types, modular packages, demonstrable main.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Mentions validation/rounding, concurrency safety, OCP for splits, and a runnable CLI/demo.

must_hit.point: Call out of scope until asked: multi-currency/FX, recurring expenses, images/notes, real payment rails, auth.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Explicitly parks FX, recurring, payments, and auth rather than designing them upfront.

probes: What functional requirements and assumptions would you lock before drawing classes?
Are EQUAL, EXACT, and PERCENT enough, or do we need SHARE, simplify, and notifications in v1?

hints.1: Start by listing users, groups, expenses, balances, and settle — then ask what is optional.
hints.2: Typical FR set is users/groups, three split types, pairwise balances, partial settle; optional simplify and passbook.
hints.3: State single currency, immutable expenses, 2-decimal money; park multi-currency, recurring, payments, and auth until asked.

phases.goal: Define the core data model: User, Group, Expense/Split, BalanceSheet, Transaction/Settlement, and SplitType.

must_hit.point: User has id, name, email and a BalanceSheet; Group has id, name, members, and optional expenses history.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Sketches User and Group with those fields and links User to BalanceSheet.

must_hit.point: Expense is immutable after build: id, description, amount, paidBy, and splits (user + computed share); settlements adjust balances rather than mutating expense shares.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Treats Expense as an append-only ledger entry and uses Settlement/Transaction for settle-up.

must_hit.point: BalanceSheet stores pairwise signed balances (Map of other user to amount) with adjustBalance; Transaction/Settlement records from, to, amount.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Shows balances[A][B]-style or signed bilateral sheet plus a Settlement/Transaction type.

must_hit.point: SplitType enum covers EQUAL, EXACT, PERCENT; Split holds user plus amount owed for that expense.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Names the enum values and a Split value object tying user to share amount.

probes: What entities do you need, and how do you represent who owes whom?
Is an expense mutable after it is added?

hints.1: List User, Group, Expense, Split, BalanceSheet, and Settlement before services.
hints.2: Expense owns computed Splits; BalanceSheet is the only place that mutates who-owes-whom.
hints.3: Expense is immutable; settleUp adjusts BalanceSheet and may append a Settlement/Transaction; passbook is expenses plus settlements a user touched.

phases.goal: Structure SplitwiseService as facade with Strategy/Factory for splits, Builder for Expense, and BalanceSheet as the mutation boundary.

must_hit.point: SplitStrategy interface with EqualSplitStrategy, ExactSplitStrategy, PercentageSplitStrategy; service must not bury if (type == EQUAL) inside Expense.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Draws SplitStrategy.calculateShares/calculateSplits and three concrete strategies used by the service.

must_hit.point: SplitwiseService facade holds users and groups maps and orchestrates addUser, createGroup/addMember, addExpense, showBalances, settleUp, optional simplifyGroupDebts.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Service API matches those methods; no split math inline in the facade.

must_hit.point: Expense built via ExpenseBuilder plus SplitStrategy; optional SplitFactory/ExpenseFactory from SplitType so callers never new concrete strategies.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Shows Builder constructing Expense after strategy produces Splits; may mention Factory from enum.

must_hit.point: Patterns map: Strategy primary; Factory optional; Builder common; Singleton for service optional (DI cleaner for tests); Observer for notify if time; Facade is the thin service API.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Can name which patterns are primary vs optional without forcing Observer/Singleton.

probes: Where does split math live versus balance mutation?
How would you add a new split type without editing Expense or the service's core flow?

hints.2: CLI → SplitwiseService → SplitStrategy → Expense/Builder → BalanceSheet; settle/simplify emit Transactions.
hints.3: SplitStrategy produces Splits; service only orchestrates and locks; BalanceSheet is the single mutator of pairwise debts.

phases.goal: Implement validation, rounding, pairwise netting, settleUp, and greedy debt simplification correctly.

must_hit.point: EQUAL divides amount among N with rounding so shares sum to total (remainder to first share); EXACT amounts must sum to total; PERCENT must sum to 100.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Describes EQUAL rounding fix, EXACT sum check, and PERCENT sum-to-100 check before updating balances.

must_hit.point: Maintain pairwise balances and net A↔B on write or read (e.g. A owes B 50 and B owes A 20 becomes A owes B 30); never leave both directions as separate non-zero lines without netting.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Explains bilateral netting and showBalances returning non-zero pairwise edges.

must_hit.point: settleUp(from, to, amount) rejects amount ≤ 0 or exceeding owed; settlements adjust balances and optionally append a Settlement/Transaction.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Validates settle amount then adjusts the pair; does not mutate historical expense shares.

must_hit.point: simplifyDebts greedy: net per user → creditors (net > 0) and debtors (net < 0) → repeatedly match largest creditor with largest debtor for min(|debt|, credit); yields ≤ N−1 transfers; exact min-transfer is NP-hard — mention, don’t implement DP unless asked.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Walks greedy simplify and states ≤ N−1 transfers plus NP-hard optimal only if pressed.

probes: How do you handle $100 split equally among 3 people?
Walk through greedy simplify and what you would say if asked for the minimum number of transfers.

hints.1: Validate EXACT/PERCENT before any balance mutation; reject atomically.
hints.2: EQUAL: two shares 33.33 and one 33.34 so totals 100.00; settle checks amount ≤ 0 and exceeds owed.
hints.3: Greedy: nets → sort creditors/debtors → settle min(|debt|, credit) until done; code that in interview time, only mention NP-hard/DP if they push optimal.

phases.goal: Show OCP for new split types and keep domain logic free of type-switches and CLI parsing.

must_hit.point: Strategy (or Split hierarchy + factory) wins over type-switch or Expense subclasses when SHARE or itemized splits appear; a giant switch fails the extensibility follow-up.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Argues adding SHARE as a new strategy without editing Expense/ExpenseService core.

must_hit.point: Keep parsing in a thin driver (EXPENSE / SHOW / SHOW u1 lines); domain logic stays in services.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Separates CLI/driver I/O from SplitwiseService and strategies.

must_hit.point: Optional later SHARE (weighted parts); Observer notify on expense/settlement only if time permits — don’t force in a time-boxed round.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Names SHARE and Observer as stretch, not blocking the happy path.

probes: Why Strategy instead of a switch on SplitType inside Expense?
Where should machine-coding input parsing live relative to domain services?

hints.1: Think about adding SHARE without touching existing expense creation paths.
hints.2: Swap EQUAL/EXACT/PERCENT via Strategy/Factory so ExpenseService stays closed for modification.
hints.3: New split type = new SplitStrategy (+ factory mapping); parser stays in the driver; Observer/SHARE only if time remains.

phases.goal: Make concurrent addExpense/settleUp on the same pair atomic without races.

must_hit.point: Two expenses updating the same pair must not race; synchronize addExpense/settleUp with a service-level lock or lock ordered user-id pairs.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Places an atomic critical section around compute-splits-then-adjust-all-pairs.

must_hit.point: ConcurrentHashMap is fine for user/group catalogs but map alone is not an atomic ledger adjust — balance updates still need a lock/critical section.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Distinguishes thread-safe maps from pairwise balance mutation atomicity.

must_hit.point: Hot group: serialize updates per group (queue or group lock); keep expense append append-only; coarse synchronized is interview-safe, fine-grained pair-ordered locks scale better if probed.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Mentions per-group serialization and tradeoff of coarse vs fine-grained locking.

probes: Is ConcurrentHashMap enough for safe balance updates?
How do you prevent two concurrent expenses from interleaving mid-update on the same pair?

hints.1: Catalog maps and ledger adjusts are different concurrency problems.
hints.2: Atomic create-expense: compute splits then adjust all pairs under one lock; don’t interleave two expenses mid-update.
hints.3: Service-wide synchronized or ordered pair locks for addExpense/settleUp; ConcurrentHashMap for users/groups only; optional per-group queue for hot groups.

tradeoffs.strong_answer: Strategy (or Split hierarchy + factory) preserves OCP when SHARE or itemized splits appear; a giant switch on SplitType inside Expense fails the extensibility follow-up.

tradeoffs.topic: Pairwise matrix vs net-only per user
tradeoffs.strong_answer: Net-only cannot answer who do I pay; pairwise or signed bilateral BalanceSheet is the interview default, with simplify collapsing the graph when asked.

tradeoffs.topic: Simplify greedy vs exact min transfers
tradeoffs.strong_answer: Greedy matching of largest creditor/debtor is what you code in ~90 min and yields ≤ N−1 transfers; exact minimum transfer count is NP-hard — mention DP/bitmask only if they push optimal.
Coarse service lock is correct and interview-safe; pair-ordered locks or per-group queues scale better under concurrent updates on hot groups — mention when concurrency is probed.

gotchas.trap: Splitting $100 equally among 3 people with naive division leaves shares that do not sum to the total.
gotchas.correction: Round to 2 decimals and absorb remainder on the first share so two get 33.33 and one gets 33.34, summing to 100.00.

gotchas.trap: Accepting invalid EXACT or PERCENT input and partially updating balances.
gotchas.correction: Validate before mutating balances (EXACT sums to amount; PERCENT sums to 100); reject the expense atomically.

gotchas.trap: Showing A owes B and B owes A as two separate non-zero lines.
gotchas.correction: Net the pair on read or on write so only the residual direction remains.

gotchas.trap: Explaining simplify like A→B 250 and B→C 200 by rewriting edges by hand.
gotchas.correction: Compute per-user nets first, then run greedy creditor/debtor matching; resulting nets depend on those nets, not ad-hoc edge rewrites.

gotchas.trap: Removing a member deletes their history or still includes them in new expenses without settling.
gotchas.correction: History stays; exclude the member from new expenses; prompt settling outstanding balances.

gotchas.trap: Relying on ConcurrentHashMap alone or interleaving two expenses mid-update.
gotchas.correction: Atomic create-expense under one lock: compute splits then adjust all pairs; catalog CHM ≠ atomic ledger adjust.

gotchas.trap: Hard-wiring SplitwiseService as a Singleton for production and tests.
gotchas.correction: Singleton is fine for a demo; prefer constructor injection in production/tests because Singleton complicates mocking.
